key_insight: InterMimicGen turns sparse human-object motion data into a self-improving training loop for humanoid robots. By making robot motion generation and tracking policy learning reinforce each other, it scales loco-manipulation beyond fixed demonstrations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human-object interactions that are sparse, varied, and not directly usable by robots. It aims to convert heterogeneous motion capture data into executable robot behaviors with coordinated whole-body and hand-object control.
method: Consolidate multiple motion-captured human-object interaction datasets into a unified training source.
Retarget human motions into humanoid robot references while preserving whole-body coordination and dexterous hand-object interactions.
Use a self-evolving loop where generated robot motion data and a tracking policy mutually improve each other over time.
impact: This is valuable for practitioners building humanoid robots because it reduces dependence on large amounts of manually curated robot demonstrations. It offers a scalable path to learning complex loco-manipulation skills from real-world human interaction data.

paper_title: InterMimicGen: Scaling Humanoid Loco-Manipulation through Self-Evolving Motion Imitation
paper_authors: Yucheng Zhang, Sirui Xu, Jinhong Li, Liuyu Bian, Anatulya Nandi
